review_candidates.description: People’s Solar Energy Fund – Executive Director Organizational Overview The People's Solar Energy Fund (PSEF) is a member-organized 501(c)3 nonprofit committed to advancing community-led renewable energy projects nationwide. Operating as a member resource commons, PSEF offers a range of capital, technical assistance, peer support services, and capacity-building and training programs for community-based organizations. Collectively, we are building a hub where frontline communities have the resources to lead the just transition. Founded in 2018 by leading environmental justice organizations, PSEF is designed to dismantle barriers to entry for historically excluded communities, support leaders of color, and build the organizational and financial infrastructure needed to ensure frontline communities have a pathway to solar ownership. To make this vision a reality, PSEF supports community-owned renewable energy projects by pairing them with accessible and affordable financing, capacity-building, and technical assistance. To date, we have supported member projects with $2M in loans and mini-grants. PSEF believes firmly that it is not only possible for frontline communities to own their own solar - it is essential. Community ownership of solar builds local self-sufficiency, strengthens resilience during disasters, creates quality jobs, reduces household energy burdens, and generates reinvestment in local economies. Organizational Structure PSEF operates as a dynamic and interconnected ecosystem, bringing together frontline community leaders nationwide to catalyze and sustain community-owned solar projects. Through shared collective knowledge, financial and technical resources, and advocacy, PSEF members are moving their communities to a just transition through community-owned solar projects. Now in its eighth year, PSEF is a flourishing network of community-led nonprofits, cooperatives, tribal entities, and municipal organizations functioning as a shared commons. Together, PSEF is building towards the collective goal of elevating equitable, locally-owned renewable energy projects as a blueprint for thriving and resilient communities. PSEF is a member-directed non-profit organization, founded on cooperative principles. It supports its members with products and offerings that advance community-accountable models of clean energy projects and is governed by a Board appointed by PSEF Members. This governance structure ensures accountability to our target communities. The Opportunity PSEF is entering its next chapter at a pivotal moment to determine the future of energy in this country. As households wake up to higher bills while the cheaper, cleaner sources of electricity that could relieve them grow less accessible, public confidence in the infrastructure meant to serve communities is eroding. Within that loss of faith lies a profound opportunity to connect communities to one another and build the collective energy infrastructure they own and govern themselves. PSEF exists to help communities seize it. And as a member-led Commons of frontline organizations, PSEF is uniquely positioned to turn rising costs and narrowing options into an undeniable case for community-led, community-owned solutions. To meet this moment, PSEF is building toward a $100M integrated capital fund for and by frontline communities, leading into a just energy future. This next chapter will require visionary leadership, disciplined execution, strong relationships, and a deep commitment to the members and communities at the center of PSEF’s mission. Core Values Justice: PSEF commits to shifting power and resources to under-resourced communities so that they have pathways to ownership, decision-making, and long-term stewardship of their resources. Equity: PSEF acknowledges the historic and present-day systemic barriers disproportionally impacting frontline communities and communities of color, and co-designs products, offerings, and pathways that seek to address those disparities. Diversity: PSEF elevates and amplifies a variety of perspectives, experiences, identities, geographies, and approaches. PSEF recognizes the value and validity of many ways, and understands the limiting view of believing in one right way to do things. Empowering Under-Resourced Communities: PSEF trusts the wisdom, leadership, and lived experiences abundant in under-resourced communities and is led by this wisdom in the mission and work. Fostering Leadership: PSEF creates pathways designed to cultivate the capacity, confidence, and skill of under-resourced communities so that they can develop, own, and lead their own renewable energy projects. Position Summary The People’s Solar Energy Fund (PSEF) seeks a visionary and enterprising Executive Director with proven capital mobilization experience to lead the organization through its next chapter of growth and impact. A central priority will be raising philanthropic and investment capital to strengthen PSEF’s financial sustainability and expand its ability to finance community-owned renewable energy projects. This leader will bring strong financial acumen, an understanding of community finance, and the ability to cultivate relationships with funders, investors, and strategic partners. Leading an operating budget of $2.2M, the Executive Director will guide PSEF through an important period of organizational and cultural evolution. This leader will work closely with the Board to translate the strategic plan into clear priorities, actionable workplans, and measurable results, ensuring member voices help shape the organization's direction. The Executive Director will also bring an enterprise-level perspective to evaluating PSEF's business models and identifying opportunities for sustainable growth. The successful candidate will be an accessible, knowledgeable, and trusted partner to PSEF's members, with a strong understanding of their needs and the challenges of advancing community-owned energy projects. Working with a remote team of 10, the Executive Director will prioritize member readiness and success, ensuring PSEF delivers meaningful value and can demonstrate the impact of its support. This leader will balance decisive executive leadership with the collaborative principles of energy democracy, bringing staff, members, and the Board together around shared priorities while building a stronger, more sustainable organization. CAPITAL RAISING & FINANCIAL STEWARDSHIP Secure funding from philanthropy, mission-aligned investors, and public sources to ensure organizational sustainability and access to capital for member projects. Oversee day-to-day operations, ensuring organizational policies, processes, and resources support efficient execution and long-term sustainability. BOARD, EXTERNAL RELATIONSHIPS & MOVEMENT LEADERSHIP Serve as a strategic partner to the Board of Directors, providing timely information, sound recommendations, and clear reporting to support effective governance and decision-making. Collaborative, Accessible, and Inclusive Leadership – Utilizes a participatory management style, balancing clear, decisive leadership with an inclusive approach that honors PSEF’s member-led governance. Builds authentic and transparent relationships with members, staff, and the Board. Communicates openly and fosters a culture of inclusion, trust, and shared ownership. Experience with financing solar projects or developing commercial solar projects is highly valued, along with familiarity with CDFIs, green banks, or loan funds.
